name: Rempi
confidence_why: Kaspruś 1942/45, the only first-hand description that states a rule, gives final stress as the basic tendency for the Mugil District languages including the A'ẹ (Rempi) dialect, with penultimate stress only in metathesised verb forms such as fíl-mi; no later source contradicts this, though Z'graggen 1971 left stress unmarked as not yet established and Dempwolff 1905's short 1901 Rempin wordlist, read by his own convention that unmarked words carry penultimate stress, leans the other way without stating any rule.
catalog_citation: Kaspruś, Aloys. 1942/1945. The Languages of the Mugil District, NE-New Guinea. Anthropos 37/40 (Heft 4-6): 711-778.
catalog_locator: sec. IV 'Notes on the Sound Attributes', 1. 'Stress', p. 734; sec. V 'Diacritical Signs and Accents', rule A and '1st Note', p. 736 (= pp. 252 and 254 of the archive.org issue scan; PDF excerpt pp. 24 and 26)
catalog_quote: [p. 734] "The basic tendency is to stress the last syllable; however, there are quite a few polysyllables which are not stressed on their last syllables. These are either exceptions in which case they will be marked by an accute accent, or they are words with an unaccented suffix or postpostion; e. g.: kalám (5); amík (90, small), but amíkta or: amík-ta (90); alót (39), but alótip or: alót-ip (valley-like; locomotion-downwards). ... The verbal suffixes of the Papuan tongues, however, take the stress; e. g.: goal-án (1063); fil-én (ib.); ahól va-ím (1064); fi-í (ib.). All genuine polysyllables are stressed on their last syllables; e. g.: ... muditín (32); teherán (97); síkelekamán (40)." [p. 736] "A) The words are basically stressed on the last syllable. Any deviation from this rule is shown by an acute accent over the syllable to be stressed, and it is only in the case of such exceptions that the accent is used to indicate stress." ... "1st Note: Concerning rule A) the Atẹ speech falls out with the rest of these languages because it stresses certain classes of polysyllables on the penultimate." ... "In conjugational forms of the verb the Atẹ have these metathesis in common with the Rempi and the Arini, and hence stress the penultimate; e. g.: (Em) fildím — (Atẹ) se'úmi, becomes in A'ẹ: fíl-mi (404)."
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the last syllable of the word (the rule is stated for all Mugil District languages, Kaspruś's Garus dialects incl. A'ẹ/Rempi among them); words carrying an unaccented suffix or postposition keep the stress on the stem's final syllable, while the Papuan verbal suffixes take the stress. Rempi-specific exception: verb conjugational forms whose suffix has undergone metathesis (Em -dim > Rempi -mi, e.g. fíl-mi 'I have come') are stressed on the penultimate, a trait Rempi shares with Atẹ (Murupi) and Arini. Non-final stress is marked by an acute accent in the vocabulary; unmarked words are final-stressed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: p. 734: polysyllables formed by reduplication or compounding 'admit a secondary stress on the accented syllables of their components with the main stress, however, on the ultimate or penultimate respectively'; reduplicated monosyllables each keep their own stress (bém sér 'one hand'). The main stress is reduced to a 'mere slur' after an interrogative particle; the question affix -e/-u carries the sentence accent.
new_statements.exceptions: (a) lexical exceptions marked with an acute accent; (b) unaccented suffixes/postpositions (-ik, -up, -ap, -yak, -ti, -to, -te, -we, -ne, -age, -vo, -ga, -ho, -a, -ya, -way, -ey, -bara, -hon, -laten) do not attract stress; (c) Rempi/Atẹ/Arini verb forms with metathesised suffixes are penult-stressed (p. 736). Later work does not confirm or refute: Z'graggen 1971 (PL C-19, p. 7) omitted stress marking 'since the stress patterning has not been well established yet', and p. 73 'None of the languages appears to be tonal'. Kaspruś 1946/49 errata alter wording on pp. 736-737 but not the stress rules.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, on citation/vocabulary forms (a 1930s missionary survey with a single A'ẹ informant, phonetic not phonemic); phrase-level effects (slur after interrogative particle, sentence accent on question affix) are described separately. The general rule A is survey-wide; only the penultimate-in-verb-forms sentence is stated for Rempi by name.
new_statements.identity_note: The only source with a stress statement, Kaspruś 1942/45, describes the language under the name "A'ẹ (A'é) or Rempi dialect", one of his "Garus dialects" (Em, A'ẹ, Atẹ, Ale, Arini). Z'graggen 1971 (PL C-19, p. 28, sec. 2.21.12.13) identifies Kaspruś's "A'e (what)" with Rempi (villages Bomasa, Deda, Kawe, Sempi), and Glottolog 5.1 attaches Kaspruś 1942/45 to remp1241; Kaspruś's own village list for the A'ẹ tribe is Rempi, Ilala, Yelbik, Baideta, Susolnak, Tana-Badimfok (p. 726). The A'ẹ data come from a single informant "of this area who knew the Em and Ate dialects as well" (p. 714 fn. 2); the older Ross/Stefansky Rempi vocabulary was lost. The p. 734/736 rule A is stated for all Mugil District languages jointly (Melanesian and Papuan); the p. 736 "1st Note" sentence is the one that names Rempi explicitly.

readall_conflicts: No stated disagreement between sources: Dempwolff 1905 states no rule for Rempin, and the only stress statements on record remain Kaspruś 1942/45 (final stress as the basic tendency, acute marks non-final exceptions; verb forms with the metathesised suffix -mi stressed on the penult, p. 736 '1st Note'). One caution rather than a conflict: under Dempwolff's p. 182 convention (unmarked = penultimate), most polysyllables in his 1896/1901 Rempin list would have been heard as penult-stressed, with only ugél, yĕtáguy, bián marked final; this is unglossed primary data gathered through Siar with a marking practice Dempwolff himself calls inconsistent ('pflegte ich oft nicht zu bezeichnen'), so it does not overturn Kaspruś's explicit rule, but it means the final-stress reading rests on a single explicit source.
